“Just as his hand will reach” is rendered “as much as he is able.”

“For opposite it he will go out” is rendered “but shall go straight out.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“The gift of his hand” is rendered “as much as one is able to give.”
The Hebrew “someone will open for him” is rendered with a passive, “shall be opened for him”; likewise “shall be shut.”
“A son of its year” is rendered “a year old.”
“Statutes of perpetuity continually” is rendered “continually by a perpetual ordinance.”
NASB adds “Thus.”
NASB has “out of his inheritance,” where the Hebrew reads “his inheritance it [is]” as a separate clause.
NASB adds “only.”
“To oppress them” is rendered “thrusting them out.”
“The rooms of holiness” is rendered “the holy chambers.”
“To make holy the people” is rendered “to transmit holiness to the people.”
The repeated “a courtyard in the corner of the courtyard” is rendered once as “in every corner … a small court.”
The Hebrew word rendered “enclosed” is uncertain; NASB renders “one measurement” as “the same size.”
“Row of stones” is rendered “row of masonry.”
“The house of those who boil” is rendered “the boiling places.”
